transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2029-06-11 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marcus (Redwood SA), Nora (Eleuthera CTO), Samir (Infra), Leah (Security)

Summary: Introductory partner discovery for a hybrid SaaS onramp: Eleuthera is evaluating a route for integrating Redwood's inference runtime across hosted + VPC private control plane. Main concerns: data residency, KMS integration, peak GPU capacity, and latency/cost tradeoffs.

Topics: scope of pilot, security requirements (SOC2/SSO/KMS), network patterns (VPC peering vs private link), GPU sizing and quantization, benchmarking plan, timeline and next steps.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Jordan, AE on the Redwood partner team, with Priya and Marcus from solutions. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Nora: good, thanks. morning from us in NYC. we're Nora, CTO at Eleuthera Systems. excited to see how Redwood could help offload some of our inferencing.
[00:15] Samir: Samir here. we'll mostly drive infra and networking questions.
[00:18] Leah: Leah, security/compliance. i've got a list of requirements i'll share.
[00:22] Priya: great thanks. quick agenda: 1) understand Eleuthera's workload and success criteria, 2) discuss deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC), 3) outline pilot/benchmark plan and next steps. sound good?
[00:30] Nora: yep that's perfect.

[00:45] Jordan: first up, can you give us a bit more color on the apps you're serving? latency targets, QPS, models?
[00:50] Nora: sure—our main use case is real-time document enrichment in our customer portal. think 200–500 qps at peak across multiple tenants, p95 latency requirement around 200ms for short prompts, some longer batch jobs for nightly embeddings. we're currently using a mix of open models—some 7B-ish and a couple custom fine-tuned 13B variants.
[01:12] Priya: okay got it. do you currently host models in-house or in cloud-managed GPU instances?
[01:17] Samir: we run most inference on rented GCP/Azure VMs and we also have a small on-prem cluster for sensitive data. cost is a big driver; we want predictable unit economics.

[01:30] Marcus: from the Redwood side, we typically recommend a hybrid pattern for that mix: hosted API for bursts and low-friction onboarding, plus a private control plane / VPC deployment for the tenant-sensitive workloads. that lets you pin the private runtime to your KMS and keep audit logs on-prem.

[01:45] Leah: so if we run the private control plane, does Redwood still manage the runtime or do we bring our own? what's the model for updates?
[01:52] Priya: good question. there are two patterns—managed-private and air-gapped on-prem. with managed-private Redwood runs the control plane but the inference nodes (GPU pool) can be in your VPC and can integrate with your KMS; we push patches via customer-approved windows. air-gapped is a more heavyweight on-prem bundle where you control rollout.

[02:15] Nora: around KMS—we use CloudKMS in GCP and have strict rotation policies. can Redwood call our KMS? or does it require key import?
[02:22] Marcus: Redwood supports external KMS integrations (GCP KMS, AWS KMS, HSMs). we can either do envelope encryption where keys never leave your KMS, or bring-your-own-key with imported key material in the private runtime. we'll need to map out key rotation windows so they don't interrupt active KV cache loads.

[02:40] Samir: firewall and peering—how does network egress work? we have strict egress rules and only a handful of IPs allowed to communicate.
[02:47] Priya: for managed-private we support VPC peering and private link-style endpoints. the runtime has a small set of outbound endpoints for telemetry; everything else stays inside your subnet. we can provide CIDRs and propose minimal firewall rules.

[03:05] Leah: audit logs and retention—our compliance needs a 7-year retention for certain records, and we need tamper-evident logs. does Redwood support that?
[03:12] Jordan: yes, Redwood Console can stream logs to your SIEM (S3, BigQuery, or Splunk). for tamper-evidence we can integrate with write-once object stores and centralized signing; we'll share the implementation notes in the SOC2 pack.

[03:30] Nora: competitors—i've spoken with NebulaCloud and TorchGrid. their pitches are similar but cost/perf tradeoffs vary. why Redwood for hybrid?
[03:39] Marcus: two reasons—1) runtime is optimized for continuous batching and prefix/KV cache which reduces per-token load without hurting latency; 2) unified tooling so you get identical control plane behaviors across hosted and private nodes—so canary deploys, model pinning, rollbacks work the same.
[03:56] Nora: okay can you give an example of latency improvements you see with KV cache?
[04:01] Priya: on realistic customer traffic we often see p95 drop from ~450ms to ~220ms for chat-like workloads after enabling prefix caching and short-context micro-batching. depends on model and sequence length but it's consistent.

[04:20] Samir: our big question is GPU sizing. we currently run mixed 80GB A100s and some older T4 pools. we need guidance on what to reserve for their 13B fine-tuned models.
[04:31] Marcus: for 13B LLMs you can usually get good perf with 80GB-class GPUs if you want single-GPU hosting for low-latency. if you intend to quantize to 4-bit and shard you can push more density onto 40–48GB cards. we'll propose a pilot topology showing both single-GPU low-latency lanes and batched high-throughput lanes.

[04:50] Nora: is quantization recommended for our fine-tuned models? any quality regression risk?
[04:55] Priya: sometimes there is a marginal quality impact with aggressive quantization—our Optimize toolkit runs evals against your prompt set and recommends quantization profiles (mixed precision, per-layer) to balance cost vs quality. we can run a QA regression check as part of the benchmark.

[05:15] Jordan: let's talk pilot scope. we propose a 4-week pilot: week 1 onboarding + infra setup, week 2 small benchmark (functional + perf), week 3 tuning and security validation, week 4 wrap and decision. does that timeline look sane?
[05:27] Nora: 4 weeks is tight but doable; we'll need internal stakeholder alignment from legal and procurement for the pilot terms.

[05:40] Leah: regarding contracts—what's the data processing agreement and is there a way to limit telemetry? we have data residency regs in EU and APAC customers.
[05:47] Jordan: we have a standard DPA and region controls for data residency. telemetry can be restricted and we can run with minimal telemetry for compliance phases—there's a tradeoff with observability but it's doable. we'll share the DPA draft.

[06:05] Samir: one more networking detail—we run strict MTU and have L7 packet inspection; will Redwood traffic break that?
[06:11] Priya: typically no; the runtime communications are standard TLS over allowed ports. if you have L7 proxies you'll need to allow websocket/streaming endpoints for streaming responses—otherwise we fall back to chunked REST.

[06:30] Nora: performance metrics we care about: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, per-request cost, and failure rates. also ability to roll back to previous model within 30 minutes.
[06:40] Marcus: rollbacks and canaries are builtin. you can set traffic splits per model version, automatic fallback to a cheaper variant if latency SLOs are violated.

[06:55] Jordan: okay jumping to concrete deliverables—I'll put together the pricing for a pilot (reserved nodes + data plane hours) and include optional burst capacity. Priya will run the benchmark. we'll also attach the SOC2 pack and our network CIDRs.

[07:10] Nora: sounds good. could you also include an example topology diagram for VPC peering and private endpoints? that helps our network team.
[07:15] Marcus: sure, we'll include a diagram and the small checklist for firewall rules.

[07:25] Leah: one of our constraints is key rotation windows—if a rotation happens and it's not synchronized, dvcs can choke because of KV cache invalidation. want to be sure we can schedule windows.
[07:33] Priya: agreed—we can surface a recommendation: rotate outside peak windows, allow a short grace period and pre-warm caches. for sensitive datasets we can avoid KV caching entirely. we'll document the recommended rotation cadence.

[07:50] Samir: about telemetry—we'd prefer logs go to our BigQuery; can Redwood stream there?
[07:55] Jordan: yes, BigQuery and S3 are supported; we'll show config snippets.

[08:05] Nora: what's the expected cost delta between 7B hosted and 13B private? rough numbers are fine.
[08:10] Marcus: rough rule: hosted per-token cost is lowest for smaller models because of shared capacity. for fine-tuned 13B on private reserved nodes you're looking at higher fixed monthly plus lower variable once fully utilized. our Optimize tool will run a cost projection for your traffic shape. we'll include a cost model in the pilot pricing doc.

[08:30] Jordan: any blockers on your side for starting the pilot?
[08:33] Nora: procurement needs a SOW and DPA; security wants SOC2 and the KMS integration notes. Samir will share VPC params.
[08:40] Samir: yes i'll extract the CIDRs and list of allowed egress IPs.

[08:45] Priya: ok operationally for the benchmark—can you share a 1% sample dataset and a representative prompt set? ideally one that includes short live prompts and some 800–1,000 token long contexts.
[08:55] Nora: yes we can prepare that, sanitized of PII.

[09:05] Jordan: timeline recap: Samir shares network details by 2029-06-14; Jordan sends SOC2 + DPA + pilot pricing by 2029-06-18; Priya schedules benchmark for week of 2029-06-24. follow-up meeting to review benchmark results week of 2029-07-01.

[09:25] Leah: can we also get a security architecture doc that explains encryption at rest/in-transit, key handling, and log retention?
[09:30] Marcus: yes will include a one-page architecture diagram and a deeper security appendix.

[09:40] Jordan: anything else?
[09:42] Nora: just one small ask—do you have reference customers who have done the hybrid private onramp recently?
[09:48] Priya: we can share case notes from a fintech and a healthcare customer (redacted). i'll include short reference call contacts if you want.

[09:58] Samir: good. for the benchmark, what's the expected telemetry footprint? we need to budget for log ingestion.
[10:03] Priya: we'll surface estimated BigQuery bytes/day and cost. it's usually small for perf tests but we'll call it out.

[10:10] Jordan: ok last piece—legal/contract. pilot SOW will be a short term thing; procurement will review. we'll aim for a minimal SOW to start.

[10:20] Nora: great. appreciate it.

[10:26] Jordan: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the pack and calendar invites.

Recap / Next steps (auto):
- Redwood: send SOC2 pack, DPA draft, VPC CIDRs, pilot pricing, and architecture diagram (Jordan)
- Eleuthera: send network details and sanitized prompt dataset (Samir/Nora)
- Redwood: schedule benchmark and send test harness (Priya)
